sources.entry: Hertzwise - Menu bar app that switches the DAC's sample rate to match each Apple Music or Tidal track, so lossless plays bit-perfect, with a per-device AutoEq headphone EQ. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/zeetabit/Hertzwise) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: Hertzwise
summary.one_liner: A Mac menu bar app that switches a DAC's sample rate to match each Apple Music or Tidal track, with per-device volume control and a headphone EQ.
use_cases: Play lossless Apple Music or Tidal tracks bit-perfect through an external DAC
Avoid macOS resampling 96 kHz tracks down to a DAC's 48 kHz setting
Apply a headphone EQ to all audio on a specific output device
Control volume on a DAC that ignores the Mac's volume setting
Keep Tidal from taking exclusive control of an audio device
summary.what_it_does: Hertzwise detects the sample rate of the track playing in Apple Music or Tidal and switches the output device's rate to match, so macOS does not resample it. Tidal rate detection reads Core Audio format logs and Tidal's player.log; Apple Music detection reads unified log messages, inherited from SyncHz. Each output device has optional switches for volume control (applied to samples for DACs that ignore the Mac's volume) and a headphone equalizer that processes audio from any app while enabled. If a DAC cannot play a requested rate, it plays the nearest supported rate and Hertzwise shows a notice. Exclusive mode is kept off.
notable: Switches DAC sample rate per track without Tidal's exclusive mode
Per-device muted process tap for volume and EQ, applied to any app
Built on SyncHz; can be installed alongside SyncHz
Self-updating after first install; MIT licensed
caveats: Not notarized; needs a one-time quarantine flag removal on install
YouTube Music support is planned, not yet available
Tidal rate switching works with exclusive mode off only
